title: Choi v. Korean Central Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC declared Complaint 2011-01 administratively out of order because it did not comply with the first sentence of BCO 43-2: the Record of the Case did not show that Korean Central Presbytery had denied Choi's complaint about its refusal to accept his charges, so the complaint was premature. No merits ruling was made.
first_summary: Sang Shul Choi complained that Korean Central Presbytery refused to accept charges he filed. The SJC dismissed the complaint as administratively out of order because it was premature: the record did not show the presbytery had denied his complaint about that refusal, so it failed BCO 43-2. No merits were reached. The vote was 17 concurring, 1 dissenting, 1 not qualified, and 5 absent.
summary: A complainant asked the SJC to review Korean Central Presbytery's refusal to accept his filed charges. The SJC held the complaint administratively out of order: the record did not show that the presbytery had denied his complaint about that refusal, so the complaint was premature under the first sentence of BCO 43-2. It made no merits determination. The vote was 17 concurring, 1 dissenting, 1 not qualified, and 5 absent; one member was not qualified because he had not read the necessary record portions.

sources.supports: Canonical complaint caption, premature filing facts, administrative out-of-order disposition under BCO 43-2, roll-call vote, and disqualification note.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2011-01, 'COMPLAINT ... MR. SANG SHUL CHOI VS. KOREAN CENTRAL PRESBYTERY' (line 11); SJC/40th Assembly (line 3); adopted vote 17 concurring, 1 dissenting, 1 not qualified, 5 absent (lines 19–23).
evidence_notes.dispute: Choi filed charges with KCP on Nov. 23, 2010; KCP (or its Clerk) did not accept them on Dec. 9, 2010; Choi filed a complaint with the GA/Stated Clerk on Jan. 7, 2011; the ROC did not show that his complaint about the refusal was denied (lines 11–13).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The complaint was administratively out of order because it did not comply with the first sentence of BCO 43-2, the record showing no denial below and therefore premature filing (lines 13–17).
evidence_notes.qualifications: Roll call includes one dissent and one member not qualified; RE Leopard was not qualified because he could not certify that he had read the necessary ROC portions under OMSJC 2.3(b), and the source applies OMSJC 2.10(e) disclosure (lines 19–25).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No incorporated decision or separate opinion text is supplied. The source records a dissent only in the roll call (line 23) without its reasoning.
